newsitem.title: INDIA: Industry body says Indian economic outlook gloomy.
newsitem.headline: Industry body says Indian economic outlook gloomy.

text.p: Declines in many Indian economic indicators in the first half of the current fiscal year point to a slowing of the economy, an Indian industry body said on Tuesday.

The 1996/97 fiscal year (April-March) will likely end with a lower rate of industrial export growth and higher fiscal and trade deficits compared with the previous year, the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM) said in a mid-year review.
Industrial growth in the current year is expected to be around 10 percent, down from the 12 percent growth achieved in fiscal 1995/96, the review said.
Data for the four months from June to September indicate a slowdown in export growth to 11 percent, compared to 28 percent over the same period last year, it said.
Economic growth has been hindered by the high cost of borrowing funds, a slump in the primary capital market, power shortages and other infrastructure bottlenecks, the review said.
Sluggish imports along with high petrol, power and freight costs also contributed, it said.
Sectors such as crude oil, textiles, fertilisers, inorganic chemicals, non-ferrous metals and electricity also performed poorly, adversely affecting overall industrial output.

The industry group said the fiscal deficit, targeted at 622.66 billion rupees, or five percent of gross domestic product, may rise to 700 billion rupees due to the government's failure to curb its spending and increase public savings.
It projected the trade deficit rising to between 6.0 billion and 7.0 billion rupees in 1996/97, fuelled by a surge in imports and a slowdown in invisible earnings.
A steady rise in inflation also played a role in worsening the trade deficit, it said.
The mid-term review said economic reforms must be continued to lessen the impact of the negative economic news.
It stressed the need to contain government expenditures, open up the insurance sector and implement direct taxation of the agricultural sector.
